interest: For a diplomatic and economic historian, this file offers valuable insight into the United States' coordinated intelligence-gathering apparatus monitoring Japan's dwindling gold and foreign exchange reserves in the critical months leading up to the Pacific War. The docket entries illuminate how the Roosevelt administration leveraged its entire diplomatic network across Central and South America following a November 1940 circular telegram to track Japanese bullion movements—such as millions of dollars in gold discharged from the Toa Maru and Terukawa Maru at Buenos Aires and Callao—and determine whether Tokyo was liquidating its last liquid reserves to settle trade balances or secure strategic commodities in anticipation of Western economic sanctions. Additionally, the February 29, 1940 memorandum highlights the close, early diplomatic coordination between State Department Far Eastern policy architects Stanley Hornbeck and Max Hamilton and the newly arrived Australian diplomat Keith Officer regarding financial credits and Pacific security.
overview: This file from State Department decimal file 894.515 (Monetary System -- Japan) contains the department's docket index sheets (List of Papers, sub-numbers 67 to 100) covering early 1940 through January 1941, together with a February 29, 1940 internal memorandum from Max M. Hamilton to Stanley K. Hornbeck concerning Australian-American discussions on credits. The docket entries comprehensively record the State Department's tracking of Japanese gold holdings, compulsory purchase laws, and international bullion shipments, with particular focus on a diplomatic dragnet across Latin America following a November 14, 1940 circular instruction. U.S. embassies and legations across Central and South America reported on whether Japanese vessels—such as the Toa Maru and Terukawa Maru—were unloading gold in ports like Callao, Buenos Aires, and Brazilian harbors, and whether these funds were destined to pay for past imports or establish exchange assets for future purchases of raw materials.

subfiles.about: A four-page State Department docket index sheet listing documents 67 through 100 filed under decimal file 894.515 concerning Japan's monetary system, gold reserves, and bullion shipments between January 1940 and January 1941.
subfiles.summary: These docket sheets record the incoming and outgoing correspondence and reports indexed under file 894.515 regarding Japanese monetary policy and gold movements during 1940 and January 1941. A major concentration of entries concerns a November 14, 1940 circular telegram dispatched to all U.S. diplomatic missions in Central and South America instructing them to report on Japanese gold imports and ascertain whether shipments were for paying existing commercial debts or establishing future purchase credits. Reports from missions across the hemisphere detail Japanese bullion shipments aboard merchant vessels such as the Toa Maru and Terukawa Maru to Peru, Argentina, and Brazil, along with accounts kept at national institutions such as the Bank of Brazil and Banque Nationale de la République d'Haïti.

subfiles.about: An internal Far Eastern Affairs memorandum informing Stanley K. Hornbeck that the complete record of his conversation with Keith Officer is being circulated to various department offices.
subfiles.from: Max M. Hamilton (Chief, Division of Far Eastern Affairs)
subfiles.summary: Max M. Hamilton, Chief of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs, informs Adviser on Political Relations Stanley K. Hornbeck that his full memorandum of conversation with Australian diplomat Keith Officer from February 10 is being sent to multiple departmental offices. Hamilton explains that although the latter portion of the conversation does not concern credits, the designated recipient offices will benefit from the broader information presented. The memorandum is initialed by Hamilton and bears the internal Far Eastern division routing code FE:MMH:REK.
